user.title: FLARE
user.description:
Sets up FLARE with a schedule and a zone per room, so it works straight away.

The schedule is the day's curve: when each phase starts and how bright and warm the light is. One is enough for most homes; add more later for floors that should differ.

A zone is usually one room. It remembers which lights FLARE is driving, and its Tick tells the room's automation when to update. Every room with lights is pre-selected. You can add, rename or remove schedules and zones at any time.

user.title: Add a FLARE schedule sensor
user.description: Adds a day-phase/curve sensor and phase-override select, grouped under a device with this name. Entities are prefixed with it too (e.g. "Living Room" -> sensor.living_room_flare). The schedule times and brightness/colour curve aren't set here - they're separate entities on the device once it's created, each starting at a sensible default and adjustable any time.

user.title: Add flare
user.description: A flare is a light for a whole room, to use from voice assistants, HomeKit or a dashboard. Turning it on with nothing else runs the room's automation, so the room comes on the way it normally would. Turning it on with a brightness or colour sets every light in the room to that, and turning it off turns every light in the room off; FLARE leaves the room alone after either until it's empty and dark.

init.title: Zones options
init.description:
Bulb models that need two-step transitions, one pattern per line. Any light whose device matches one of these patterns is routed into two-step transitions automatically, with no label needed — the box starts pre-filled with the models shipped with the integration, and you can add to it or remove from it freely.

Patterns are matched case-insensitively against “manufacturer model”, and * is a wildcard, e.g. *TRADFRI bulb* or IKEA*. Clearing the box entirely falls back to the shipped defaults, so it can't quietly switch off detection.

Once you save your own list it stays as you left it — a later release adding a newly discovered bulb won't change it.

Each zone's Tick fires once per update interval, a gap apart from the next zone's, so rooms don't all send at the same moment. A change smaller than the minimum brightness or colour temperature change isn't sent at all.

data_description.tick_interval: How often each zone ticks, in minutes.
data_description.tick_gap: Seconds between one zone's Tick and the next. Shrinks automatically if the zones wouldn't otherwise fit in the interval.
data_description.min_brightness_change: A light within this percentage of its target brightness is left alone.
data_description.min_color_temp_change: A light within this many mireds of its target colour temperature is left alone.
